mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility rises monotonically from -28.6 to -19.6 across the four weekly means, so a growing share of the workforce is commuting; commuter footfall is a direct input to weekday retail-and-recreation trips, which raises RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES weekly mean rose from -28.6 at t-3w to -19.6 at t-0w, a 9.0-point gain
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is at or below its last-28-day mean of -13.0 while WORKPLACES keeps rising week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls every week (9.6, 7.9, 7.4, 6.9), showing stay-at-home adherence decaying; once the residential mean crosses below 7.5, home time no longer absorbs discretionary hours and out-of-home retail-and-recreation trips accelerate within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean below 7.5 in two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 9.6 at t-3w to 6.9 at t-0w, crossing 7.5 at t-1w
failure_condition: In the two weeks after RESIDENTIAL prints below 7.5, RETAIL_REC fails to improve versus its prior two-week mean in more than half of observations.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility climbs from -51.0 to -45.6, consistent with relaxed capacity caps on public transport; once the transit mean crosses above -46.0, commuters resume transit-linked discretionary trips and RETAIL_REC rises over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above -46.0 after three weeks below it
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -51.0 at t-3w to -45.6 at t-0w, the first print above -46.0
failure_condition: Two weeks after TRANSIT exceeds -46.0, the RETAIL_REC weekly mean is at or below -13.0.

mechanism_narrative: Workplace and transit recovery reinforce each other: WORKPLACES gains supply commuters while TRANSIT gains supply the means to reach high streets, and only their joint improvement lifts discretionary footfall enough to raise RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve week-on-week for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:both improved in each of the last three weekly transitions (WORKPLACES -28.6 to -19.6; TRANSIT -51.0 to -45.6)
failure_condition: In weeks when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve together, RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the following four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility deteriorates sharply (-9.4 to -18.0) while the RETAIL_REC improvement decelerates (+2.6, +0.5, +1.9), so the breadth of out-of-home activity is narrowing; when park usage sits 5 or more points below its four-week mean, RETAIL_REC's next two-week mean is lower than the last four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean more than 5 points below its own four-week mean
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS four-week mean is -12.8 and the t-0w print is -18.0, a 5.2-point shortfall
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean exceeds its last-28-day mean of -13.0 while PARKS stays 5 or more points below its four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: Winter onset in Delhi lowers outdoor activity: PARKS falls to -18.0 while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated at 6.9 above baseline, indicating trips are being cancelled rather than relocated indoors, which drags RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean below -15.0 while RESIDENTIAL remains above 5.0
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped 8.6 points over the window while RESIDENTIAL stayed positive at 6.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is higher than -13.0 even though PARKS remains below -15.0 and RESIDENTIAL stays above 5.0.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM is the only category above baseline (6.3 to 7.4) and is flat-to-rising, showing that routine in-person errands are fully normalized; that normalization lowers the perceived cost of discretionary errands, so RETAIL_REC rises within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM held between +6.3 and +7.4 across all four weekly means
failure_condition: In the week after GROCERY_PHARM prints at or above +7.0, RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the prior week.

mechanism_narrative: Rising TRANSIT together with falling RESIDENTIAL is the signature of containment measures unwinding; when transit gains at least 3 points week-on-week in the same week residential drops at least 0.4 points, restriction-driven suppression of retail-and-recreation is lifting and RETAIL_REC rises over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves 3 or more points week-on-week in the same week RESIDENTIAL falls 0.4 or more points
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT gained 5.4 points and RESIDENTIAL lost 2.7 points over the four-week window
regime_hint: loosening restrictions with no new lockdown announced
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is at or below -13.0 in periods when TRANSIT gains 3 or more points and RESIDENTIAL falls 0.4 or more points simultaneously.
